solid.explanation: "Solid" means "solid", as in strong and well built. To describe a person you can trust, it means "reliable": "en solid mand" (a reliable man).

solrig.explanation: "Solrig" means "sunny". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "rig" (rich), so it is literally "sun-rich". To say the weather is sunny, add "t": "Det er solrigt i dag" (It is sunny today).

solrigt.explanation: "Solrigt" means "sunny". To describe the weather, use it after "det er" (it is): "Det er solrigt" (It is sunny). It is the form of "solrig" that goes before "vejr" (weather): "solrigt vejr" (sunny weather).

solskin.explanation: "Solskin" means "sunshine". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "skin" (shine). The verb "at skinne" (to shine) goes with the sun: "Solen skinner" (The sun is shining).

solskinsvejr.explanation: "Solskinsvejr" means "sunny weather". It is built from "solskin" (sunshine) and "vejr" (weather). To say you do something in sunny weather, use "i" (in): "Vi spiser ude i solskinsvejr" (We eat outside in sunny weather).

solsystemet.explanation: "Solsystemet" means "solar system". It is built from "sol" (sun) and "system" (system). To say a planet circles the sun, use the verb "at kredse" (to orbit): "Jorden kredser om solen" (The Earth orbits the sun).

som.explanation: "Som" means "that" when it joins two parts of a sentence. To say which person you mean, say: "manden, som bor her" (the man who lives here). To say what someone was when younger, it means "as": "Som barn boede jeg i Aarhus" (As a child I lived in Aarhus). To compare, it means "like": "Hun synger som en engel" (She sings like an angel).

som følge af.explanation: "Som følge af" means "as a result of". To name the cause of something, put the cause after it: "Skolen lukkede som følge af snestormen" (The school closed as a result of the snowstorm). To say "because of" in plain terms, use "på grund af" (because of): "Toget var forsinket på grund af sne" (The train was delayed because of snow).

som helst.explanation: "Som helst" means "any". To say anyone may do something, add it after "hvem" (who): "Hvem som helst kan komme" (Anyone can come). After "noget" (something) in a sentence with "ikke" (not), it means "at all": "Jeg ved ikke noget som helst" (I know nothing at all).

som om.explanation: "Som om" means "as if". To describe how someone acts, say: "Han opfører sig, som om han ejer stedet" (He acts as if he owns the place).

som regel.explanation: "Som regel" means "usually". Literally, it is "as a rule". To say something is always true with no exceptions, use "altid" (always) instead: "Jeg drikker altid kaffe" (I always drink coffee).

somme tider.explanation: "Somme tider" means "sometimes". Literally, it is "some times". Danish also allows the spelling "sommetider" (sometimes) as one word.

sommertid.explanation: "Sommertid" means "daylight saving time". It is built from "sommer" (summer) and "tid" (time). To say you move the clock forward, say: "Vi stiller uret frem" (We set the clock forward).

sommetider.explanation: "Sommetider" means "sometimes". It is built from "somme" (some) and "tider" (times). Danish also allows the spelling "somme tider" (sometimes) as two words.

sorg.explanation: "Sorg" means "sorrow", which also covers grief. For everyday sadness that is not grief, say: "Jeg er ked af det" (I am sad).

sort.explanation: "Sort" means "black". For work done without telling the tax authorities, it is used in "sort arbejde" (undeclared work): "Det er sort arbejde" (That is undeclared work).

sov godt.explanation: "Sov godt" means "sleep well". It is built from "sov" (sleep) and "godt" (well). To ask the next morning whether someone slept well, say: "Har du sovet godt?" (Did you sleep well?)

spaghetti.explanation: "Spaghetti" means "spaghetti". To say you want some, leave out "en": "Jeg vil have spaghetti" (I want spaghetti). To name a portion, use "en tallerken" (a plate): "en tallerken spaghetti" (a plate of spaghetti).

spansk.explanation: "Spansk" means "Spanish". It comes from "Spanien" (Spain). To say you are learning the language, say: "Jeg lærer spansk" (I am learning Spanish).

spartansk.explanation: "Spartansk" means "plain", as in without comfort or extras. It comes from "Sparta", the ancient Greek city known for its hard way of life.

speciel.explanation: "Speciel" means "special". Danish ends it in "-el", not "-al" as English does. To say someone is a little odd, use it about the person: "Han er lidt speciel" (He is a bit odd).

specifik.explanation: "Specifik" means "specific". Its opposite is "generel" (general): "et generelt spørgsmål" (a general question).

spegepølse.explanation: "En spegepølse" means "a salami". To say what is in your packed lunch, say: "Der er spegepølse i min madpakke" (There is salami in my packed lunch).
